title: Variants of vision encoder
reading: The slide surveys the main training paradigms used to produce vision encoders, each tagged with a canonical model and its authors: supervised learning (ViT, Dosovitskiy et al.), masked modeling (MAE, He et al.), auto-encoding (VQVAE, Van den Oord et al.), self-distillation (DINO, Caron et al.), and multimodal learning (CLIP, Radford et al.). A caption indicates an accompanying visual comparing how popular each of these encoder types is within multimodal LLMs.

visuals.description: A figure captioned 'Popularity of different vision encoders in Multimodal LLMs', presumably comparing usage frequency across the five encoder families listed.
visuals.assertion: Vision encoder families differ substantially in adoption within multimodal LLMs.

concepts.name: ViT (supervised learning)
concepts.why_it_matters: Baseline transformer vision encoder trained with labels.

concepts.name: MAE (masked modeling)
concepts.why_it_matters: Self-supervised pretraining by reconstructing masked patches.

concepts.name: VQVAE (auto-encoding)
concepts.why_it_matters: Discrete latent auto-encoding used for tokenized visual representations.

concepts.name: DINO (self-distillation)
concepts.why_it_matters: Label-free representation learning via teacher-student distillation.

concepts.name: CLIP (multimodal learning)
concepts.why_it_matters: Image-text contrastive training yields encoders aligned with language, common in MLLMs.

verbatim_spans: Popularity of different vision encoders in Multimodal LLMs
